source.title: Make Continual Learning Stronger via C-Flat
source.authors: Ang Bian; Wei Li; Hangjie Yuan; Cheng-Wei Yu; Mang Wang; Zi-Xiang Zhao; Ao-Jun Lu; Peng-Liang Ji; Tao Feng

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation or garbling that prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies continual-learning performance and loss-landscape flatness. Its results concern task accuracy and forgetting, not the claim versions about fitting random labels, natural-label train/test gaps, width, convolutional inductive bias, optimizer generalization on standard tasks, batch size, dropout, sharpness measures tracking generalization gaps, or removing memorized training examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports accuracy gains and flatter loss landscapes after applying C-Flat in continual-learning settings. Those accuracy results concern learning across sequential tasks and forgetting, not held-out generalization under the specified versions. Hessian values and traces compare C-Flat with SGD but do not measure a training/test generalization gap. Table 1 includes isolated decreases for C-Flat on ImageNet-100 B50_Inc25 Replay and Tiny-ImageNet B50_Inc25 iCaRL; these are continual-learning results outside the versions.
record.test_reason: No result tests V1–V8. The closest comparison, V7, requires magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance and train/test generalization gaps. This study instead measures Hessian curvature and continual-learning accuracy or forgetting. Its optimizer comparisons do not compare adaptive methods with SGD, as V4 requires.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' main conclusion: C-Flat is a broadly applicable continual-learning optimization framework that improves performance and induces flatter measured landscapes. Qualify the performance summary as improvements in most tested combinations: Table 1 includes two decreases and one tie, despite stronger consistency language in the conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares continual-learning optimization methods and task-level performance; it does not implement the original study recipes or measures represented by the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: C-Flat's task-level accuracy varies with dataset, incremental scenario, continual-learning baseline, and iteration ratio. The study reports that its accuracy is not oversensitive to λ and ρ within a reasonable range.

fits_no_version.finding: For MEMO on CIFAR-100 B0_Inc10, C-Flat lowers maximal Hessian eigenvalues from 67.48 to 28.11 at epoch 50 and from 21.07 to 6.25 at epoch 150. Reported traces fall from 670.36 to 429.90 and from 321.36 to 97.36, respectively (Section 4.3, Figure 2). Neither measure establishes V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: C-Flat reduces measured loss-landscape curvature in class-incremental learning.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 1 reports improved average incremental accuracy in most baseline/dataset/scenario combinations, with two decreases and one tie. These comparisons measure C-Flat's continual-learning performance rather than any listed version.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding C-Flat usually improves average class-incremental accuracy across the tested continual-learning methods.

record.problems: No error bars or statistical significance tests are reported. Results are for class-incremental continual learning, so their accuracy measures do not establish the standard train/test generalization effects in the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were eligible: reported task-accuracy and forgetting outcomes do not measure any listed version's behavior. No results were omitted from an otherwise eligible version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization using the same architecture and training recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Magnitude-aware sharpness tracking train/test gaps at similarly low training loss, including comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's relation from tests to discusses; T6 and the empty eligible-row set are appropriate. The gate note mislocates the exceptions: Replay decreases on ImageNet-100 B50_Inc10 (63.89 to 63.60), and iCaRL decreases on ImageNet-100 B50_Inc25 (77.25 to 76.22). FOSTER ties on ImageNet-100 B50_Inc25 (87.81). Continual learning itself is not the exclusion; the measured interventions and outcomes do not match the listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization on image or language tasks.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the train/test generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
